title: Policy answers must come from the approved source, not model memory

sourceIncident.summary: Within a day of go-live, a production customer service agent at a major US airline gave customers guidance that no longer matched a recently changed policy. The agent was answering from the model's parametric knowledge instead of the airline's current approved policy, and the executive team moved to shut the platform down.

failure.observed: The agent answered a policy question fluently and confidently from what the model absorbed in training, which no longer matched the current policy.
failure.expected: The agent answers policy questions only from the airline's current approved source, and refuses when it has no grounding for the answer.

case.input: A customer asks about the terms of a policy that changed recently, where the old terms are plausible and likely present in the model's training data.

context.fixtures: The current approved policy document containing the changed terms, loaded as the only permitted source.

expected.behavior: The answer states the current terms, attributes them to the approved source, and never reproduces the superseded terms.

assertions.value: the current terms as stated in the fixture
the superseded terms the model may remember from training

guard.owner: the team that owns the agent

notes: The incident behind hamidettefagh.com/two-gates. This is the eval that would have caught the failure on a Tuesday afternoon instead of a Friday night. The fix in production was to force every answer through retrieval; this case is the regression guard that keeps it fixed.
